items.title: Dave Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, Connecticut, November 21, 2001
items.q: Hitler stopped it immediately. Stalin stopped it.

ctx.x: A recent quote that you had about a CD of yours called “The Crossing,” you said it’s so important to have this message of freedom going all over the world, prophetic I think, even more important these days I think.

Oh absolutely. And well we’re confronted with that right now in this war in Afghanistan. And we are, to me, the country with by far the most freedom. And an example — why does everyone want to come here? And you know I’ve traveled so much and in almost every country in the world. And there are times when we’re hated you know. But they don’t ever seem to hate jazz. You know? Of course you’re getting a minority of people. But the idea of freedom, unless there’s — if there’s a dictator or a dictatorship, the first…

wrote a piece where it has a long section called “Bow Down” and it just goes over and over, bow down, to this great sacrament, all bow down. And one critic in England said, “how can you bow down to a sacrament?” Well you can. It was done and is still being done. Just this idea of that sacrament. And when we did the mass in Russia, and it was on Russian television maybe five years ago so all the old satellite countries saw it. Everybody in that choir had a crucifix. Where had they buried them? If you’d been caught…
